name: Storybook
tagline: Workshop for building, documenting and testing UI components in isolation.
hook: Carries a Learned User Preferences section recording corrections from maintainers.
summary: Storybook covers repository structure, architecture, commands, pull requests, and tests. Two sections govern the guide itself: one requires updates when the project changes, and another records maintainer preferences learned during earlier work.

techniques.title: A section of accumulated corrections
techniques.body: Learned User Preferences records five maintainer corrections: use worktrees for parallel work, avoid premature helpers, keep long interaction tests readable instead of forcing DRY, put story descriptions above the meta const, and preserve telemetry strings across renames.
techniques.quote: Keep e2e and long interaction tests as a readable continuous flow; do not force DRY with loops or heavy helpers when repetition is clearer.

techniques.title: The file names itself as canonical
techniques.body: Other agent entrypoints are directed to reference this file rather than duplicate it, and the agent is instructed to update it when architecture, commands, versions or release flows change. A Maintenance Rules section states both in full.
techniques.quote: This file is the canonical instruction source for coding agents. Files like `CLAUDE.md` should point here instead of duplicating instructions.

techniques.title: Principles labelled as observed failure modes
techniques.body: Code Authoring Principles comes from failures seen in agent changes. It asks for a throwaway probe before encoding environment assumptions, prefers static checks where possible, and avoids tests for guarantees already enforced by types or linting.
techniques.quote: These are recurring failure modes in agent-authored changes to this repo. Apply them when writing or reviewing code, not just when asked.

techniques.title: An inverted default for component tests
techniques.body: For React components the file directs behavior, accessibility and interaction assertions into stories with play functions, and reserves unit test files for pure utilities, hooks and non-React modules.

techniques.title: A ban on direct global assignment in tests
techniques.body: Assigning a global directly is prohibited, with the mechanism given: Vitest does not restore it, so the assignment leaks into unrelated test files and produces order-dependent flakiness. The replacement API and its cleanup call are both named.
techniques.quote: Direct assignment leaks across tests and files — Vitest does not restore it — so it silently changes behavior in unrelated tests and creates order-dependent flakiness.

techniques.title: Commands the agent should not run
techniques.body: Two commands are listed under a Commands To Avoid heading, with the reason that they start long-running development servers, which the file describes as the wrong default for an agent.

steal: Keep a section for corrections that came up in review. It is the cheapest way to stop repeating the same feedback.
Name the commands that start long-running processes and tell the agent not to run them.
When a test rule exists because of a framework behavior, state the behavior. "Vitest does not restore it" is what makes the rule stick.
If your repo has several agent entrypoints, name one canonical file and make the rest point at it.
outline: How To Work In This Repo
